stories.title: 18 Year-Old from the Bronx Starts Nonprofit to Sponsor School Children in Ghana
stories.label: people
stories.summary: Max Owobu, an 18-year-old high school senior from the Bronx, started his own nonprofit to help sponsor school children in Ghana. While juggling exams and college applications like any other senior, he also found time to travel to Ghana to see the work in person. His organization helps cover the costs that keep kids in the classroom. It's a heartwarming reminder of what young people can build when they decide to help others. His generosity is already changing lives on the other side of the world.
stories.why_good: A real, completed act of youth-led generosity that is already helping children access education.

stories.title: Vietnam Swiftly Protects Forests Containing the Last of the World's Most-Endangered Monkey
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: Vietnam has just set aside about 7,500 acres of stunning limestone mountains and forest to create a new conservation reserve. It's home to the Delacour's langur, one of the rarest primates on Earth, with only a small population left in the wild. This protection didn't take years of red tape -- officials moved quickly once they understood how urgent the threat was. Now these striking black-and-white monkeys, along with the wild landscape they depend on, have a real safeguard for the future. It's a rare case of conservation happening at the speed the crisis actually demanded.
stories.why_good: A real, finalized land protection that directly saves a critically endangered species from extinction -- not a proposal, an accomplished designation.

stories.title: Researchers Unearth a Clay Tablet Inscribed With the World's Oldest Peace Treaty
stories.label: peace
stories.summary: Archaeologists have uncovered an ancient clay tablet recording what's believed to be the world's oldest surviving peace treaty, a pact between ancient Egypt and the Hittite Empire. Written in Akkadian more than 3,000 years ago, the tablet describes lasting peace and brotherhood between the two nations after years of conflict. It's a remarkable reminder that even history's fiercest rivals once found a way to lay down their weapons and choose cooperation instead. The discovery gives historians a rare, tangible piece of humanity's long story of choosing peace over war.
stories.why_good: It's a genuine archaeological discovery documenting a real historical peace agreement, offering an uplifting, non-political story about reconciliation between former enemies.
